hypothesis: The first-person view builder stops because weapon 78 never passes its asynchronous fastfile readiness gate; if the missing signed ak47_mp.ff is made available, the registration and model-resolution calls should become reachable.

source_side.limit: snapshot_source is a server-side send record; it is not proof that the client accepted every snapshot.

native_path.view_builder: 0x5903F0 selects cg+0x3F8=78 and sees per-ID lookup word 0; 0x5904BD returns while queue item (78,0) is pending.
native_path.queue_processor: 0x59AED0 is called from frame sites 0x515894 and 0x5C2A4D/0x5C2A6C; it reads 0x82CA590 queue and clears it at 0x59B23A. In r744 the queue enter/clear hooks each exceeded 13,000 hits during one active session.
native_path.file_check: 0x4A0410 builds %s%c%s%s.ff from base path '.' and asset name, attempts a direct file open, then optional filesystem fallback. During r744 the fallback pointer [0x779570C] was zero; the captured asset input was ak47_mp. This explains why r744 repeatedly skips past 0x59B091 without registration in the observed process.

profile_safety.classification: Both changed databases had unchanged schema/table row counts and integrity=ok; accounts revision/updated and one profiles blob/hash changed. This is a normal client write, preserved in ignored r743-after-local.sqlite3 and r745-after-local.sqlite3 before restoring the exact baseline for repeatability.

conclusion: The missing first-person weapon in r743 is blocked before typed model resolution at the per-weapon cache/fastfile availability path. A verified source fastfile reached registration once in r745, but produced error 174 and did not render a gun. The error source and whether other bundles or registration assumptions are required remain open. Real connection is verified; restored loadout UI was separately observed previously; first-person weapon, shooting, and full acceptance remain unproven.
